definitions.explanation: The quality of speaking powerfully and persuasively. Also used figuratively to describe things that communicate something strongly without words.

examples.japanese: {彼|かれ}は{雄弁|ゆうべん}な{人|ひと}だ。
この{数字|すうじ}が{問題|もんだい}の{深刻|しんこく}さを{雄弁|ゆうべん}に{物語|ものがた}っている。
examples.english: These numbers eloquently tell of the severity of the problem.

examples.japanese: {沈黙|ちんもく}は{時|とき}として{言葉|ことば}よりも{雄弁|ゆうべん}に{気持|きも}ちを{伝|つた}えることがある。
examples.english: Silence can sometimes convey feelings more eloquently than words.

notes:
USAGE:
{雄弁|ゆうべん} can describe a person's speaking ability or, more commonly in modern usage, things that powerfully communicate a message. The figurative use — {雄弁|ゆうべん}に{物語|ものがた}る (to tell eloquently) — is especially frequent.

The well-known proverb {雄弁|ゆうべん}は{銀|ぎん}、{沈黙|ちんもく}は{金|きん} ("Speech is silver, silence is gold") uses this word.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {雄弁|ゆうべん}に{物語|ものがた}る (to tell eloquently; to speak volumes)
- {雄弁|ゆうべん}な{演説|えんぜつ} (eloquent speech)
- {雄弁|ゆうべん}{家|か} (eloquent speaker; orator)
- {雄弁|ゆうべん}は{銀|ぎん}、{沈黙|ちんもく}は{金|きん} (speech is silver, silence is gold)
